structure: For marker M and visit t, M_it = B_Mi + E_Mit. Stable vectors have covariance [[4, 3.2], [3.2, 4]]. Each visit-deviation vector has covariance [[1, 0.3], [0.3, 1]]. Stable and deviation blocks are independent; deviation vectors are independent across visits; persons are independent. Gaussian block distributions and a common within-visit deviation correlation of 0.3 complete an illustrative point scenario.

parameter_provenance.basis: Measurement means are zero and visit deviations have mean zero, so stable-component means are zero.
Exact Pearson correlation of stable X and Y components.
Illustrative unmeasured relationship, chosen equal at both visits. Independent visits do not imply independent markers within a visit.
Convenient sampling distribution; the records constrain moments and independence, not distributional shape.

parameter_provenance.value: Stable-component vector independent of visit-deviation vectors; visit-deviation vectors mutually independent; persons independent.

parameter_provenance.basis: At either visit, each marker has variance 4 + 1 = 5.

requested_estimands.name: change_correlation
requested_estimands.basis: Stable components cancel in changes. Independent visits give change variances 2 and change covariance 0.3 + 0.3 = 0.6. Thus Pearson correlation is 0.6/2 = 0.3, conditional on the chosen within-visit deviation correlation.

requested_estimands.name: same_visit_correlation
requested_estimands.basis: At either visit, covariance is 3.2 + 0.3 = 3.5 and both variances are 5, giving 3.5/5 = 0.7. The deviation covariance is not supplied by the records.

requested_estimands.name: cross_visit_correlation
requested_estimands.basis: Independence removes cross-visit deviation covariance and all stable-deviation cross terms. Cov(X_visit1, Y_visit2) = 3.2, while both measurement variances equal 5; therefore correlation is 3.2/5 = 0.64, independently of Gaussian shape or within-visit deviation correlation.

limitations: These are artificial population constraints and a mathematical scenario, not biomedical validation.
The records do not identify either visit's within-visit deviation covariance. Equality of those covariances across visits is also an assumption.

With a common deviation correlation r in [-1, 1], change correlation equals r and same-visit correlation equals (3.2 + r)/5. Thus their admissible ranges are [-1, 1] and [0.44, 0.84], respectively; cross-visit correlation remains 0.64.
The supplied units do not imply unit marginal variance: the records require measurement variance 5. No additional standardization is applied.
Finite random samples will fluctuate around the population quantities. The generator does not rescale, select, sort, or reject persons to enforce sample moments.
checks_actually_performed: Analytically checked covariance validity: stable-component covariance eigenvalues are 7.2 and 0.8; visit-deviation covariance eigenvalues are 1.3 and 0.7, all positive.
Algebraically checked measurement variances, change variances, and the three population Pearson correlations.
Inspected the source for one row per person, integer identifiers, exact requested column order, seeded randomness, and independent latent draws without sample-moment adjustment.
No code execution or empirical simulation checks were performed.
